items.prompt: Three URLs agree: n8n's release notes, docs.n8n.io, and a mirror of the release notes on a community CDN. How many voices?
options: One — all three belong to the n8n independence group; mirrors are recorded, never counted
Two — the CDN is a different host
items.explanation: Independence is modelled by publisher/independence groups, and two pages from one publisher count as one voice: groups, not addresses. (obj-13-a)

items.prompt: Why does a search-engine discovery source NOT count toward the two-voice rule?
options: Discovery sources cost too many credits

One engine returning three pages is one engine's opinion of relevance — a hit is a lead; the pages it points at are fetched through the allowlist and counted by their own publishers (counts_as_independent: false)
items.explanation: The engine finds; it never vouches — otherwise one autocomplete becomes your second source. (obj-13-a)

items.prompt: Two qualified, independent sources DISAGREE on the same fact. What does the system do?
options: ESCALATE [source_conflict] with both quotes and anchors preserved — never average, never pick; the distinction needs a human
Average the two positions into a careful middle claim
Wait one scan cycle and publish whichever repeats
items.explanation: Averaging manufactures false consensus; conflict is the most informative state the verify phase can produce, and it routes to a human with both quotes intact. (obj-13-b)

items.prompt: Which page state is NOT one of the four disqualifiers?
options: Addressed to the operator — the page talks to the system
Unreachable — fetch failed or page gone
Stale — a snapshot failing the subject's freshness window
items.explanation: The four: single voice, stale, unreachable, addressed-to-the-operator. Popularity is orthogonal to evidence. (obj-13-b)
